title: Distributed Transactions

searches.query: "Distributed Transactions" system design interview failures atomicity
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: Gray and Lamport: Consensus on Transaction Commit
sources.supportRationale: Atomic commit problem, classic 2PC blocking and distinction from fault-tolerant consensus-based commit.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Two-phase transactions
sources.supportRationale: Prepared participant state, durable storage and intended external transaction-manager integration.

sources.title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Transactional outbox
sources.supportRationale: Local state/event atomic publication intent and duplicate-consumer considerations.

sources.title: Microsoft Azure: Saga distributed transactions pattern
sources.supportRationale: Modern orchestration/choreography and workflow recovery choices; no inference of automatic isolation or guaranteed compensation success.

sources.title: Herlihy and Wing: Linearizability
sources.supportRationale: Original operation-history correctness condition and comparison with other conditions.

sources.title: Amazon Builders’ Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter
sources.supportRationale: Timeout uncertainty, safe repeated effects, retry amplification, bounded retries and jitter; URL redirects to the author's AWS Builder Center article.

scenarios.theme: Debit commits but credit fails. What do you change?
scenarios.assumptions: The API promised a final atomic transfer, but services independently commit their own databases. What will you do and why?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Revisit ownership and use one supported atomic boundary or distributed transaction meeting the required visibility/failure contract

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Distributed commit adds coupling and can retain resources during failure

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Atomically store the state change and outbox entry locally, relay it durably, and make consumer effects duplicate-safe using stable identity

scenarios.theme: A pending transfer is stuck for hours. Who fixes it?
scenarios.assumptions: Every service retries locally, but none owns reconciliation across the workflow. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Transactions to recovery owner.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A pending transfer is stuck for hours. Who fixes it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Assign a durable workflow/recovery owner with an explicit state machine, deadlines, idempotent steps, reconciliation checks and manual escalation

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Central recovery ownership adds an operational component; choreography still needs equivalent responsibility and observability

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Blindly replaying all actions can duplicate external effects or contradict completed steps.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to saga, outbox; interview frequency is not claimed.
